prompt: The program below runs to completion. What does it print, and why?

snippets.label: program

options.text: It prints positive, because both if statements are evaluated and only the first condition is true.
options.feedback: Correct. The two if statements are independent: each condition is tested, the first is true and the second is false, so label is "positive" when it is printed.

options.text: It prints positive, because the first matching if ends the branch and the later if is skipped like an elif.
options.feedback: Half credit. The printed output is correct, but the explanation is not: separate if statements are all evaluated, and here the second condition simply does not match.
options.partial_reason: The printed output is right for this input, but the stated reason is wrong: the later if is not skipped the way an elif is; it is tested on its own and is false here.

options.text: It stops with a NameError, because value > 0 produces a number and only a literal True or False can control an if statement.
options.feedback: A comparison produces a bool, and an if tests any expression for truthiness. The first condition is true, so label is assigned and no NameError occurs.

options.text: It prints huge, because the name label is bound to whichever label text appears last in the source.
options.feedback: Only the first branch runs here, so label is never reassigned. The text "huge" is present in the source but is not executed, and source order by itself does not change a name.

options.text: It prints huge, because a true if makes the next if statement run as though it were an else branch.
options.feedback: A later if is not an else branch; it has its own condition, value > 100, which is false for value = 10, so label stays "positive".

explanation: Both if statements are independent. value is 10, so the first condition (value > 0) is true and label becomes "positive". The second condition (value > 100) is false, so label is not changed. The program prints positive.

verification.rationale: Running the primary snippet with no input writes "positive\n" and exits 0, which supports the correct option: the first condition matches and the second does not. It does not show that independent if statements can never behave like elif for other inputs, and it does not validate the explanations in the other options.
verification.limitations: One deterministic input only. Rewrite equivalence, asymptotic complexity and whether the half-credit option is genuinely half right are not established by execution.
